source_semantics.history_rule: Restoring never rewrites history; it creates a new revision from the selected historical content.
source_semantics.current_revision: The Restore control is disabled for the currently selected revision.
source_semantics.confirmation: Restore revision r{revision} of {key} as a new revision?
source_semantics.mutation: PromptStore.Restore replays the selected historical snapshot as a new revision and then reloads the selected prompt while preserving the result message.
source_semantics.failure: Restore failures are surfaced truthfully and never report success.

laravel_adaptation.append_only_fix: Restore passes forceRevision=true so a restore always creates a new revision even when the target snapshot equals current state; normal Save deduplication is unchanged.
laravel_adaptation.confirmation: Browser confirmation is required before the form submits.
laravel_adaptation.current_revision_guard: Current revision control is disabled in the UI and direct current-version POST returns 409.

security.revision_lookup: revision must belong to the tenant-scoped selected template
security.locked_builtin: validation failure with no revision or audit mutation

persistence.history: Existing revisions remain unchanged; restore appends change_type=restored.
persistence.actor: The authenticated tenant member is stored as updated_by_user_id, revision actor_user_id, and audit actor_user_id.

proofs: exact canonical operation identity and source semantics
explicit guarded POST route and controller wiring
truthful Restore control with canonical marker and confirmation
current revision disabled and direct current-version POST rejected
historical snapshot replayed as a new revision
repeated restore of an already-current snapshot still appends a new revision
authenticated actor and audit provenance persisted
guest, permission, tenant, direct-key, missing-revision, and locked-built-in boundaries fail closed
separately owned New, Save, Back, and route operations remain excluded
